lessons.title: Rectangle dimensions and the square-unit grid
lessons.objective: Identify the length and width of a rectangle and count the number of unit squares it covers.
must_establish: The length and width are the two perpendicular side measurements of a rectangle
The number of unit squares covering a rectangle is found by counting rows and columns
Area is reported in square units

lessons.title: Applying area = length x width
lessons.objective: Calculate the area of a rectangle by multiplying its length by its width.
must_establish: The formula area = length x width gives the number of unit squares in a rectangle
Multiplication of the two side lengths replaces counting squares
The result is stated with square-unit labels

lessons.title: Finding a missing side from area
lessons.objective: Find an unknown side length of a rectangle given its area and the other side length.
must_establish: Area divided by a known side length gives the unknown side length
The relationship area = length x width can be rearranged to solve for a missing dimension

lessons.title: Decomposing compound shapes into rectangles
lessons.objective: Split a compound shape made from rectangles into non-overlapping rectangles and identify the dimensions of each part.
must_establish: A compound rectangular shape can be partitioned into rectangles that do not overlap and cover the whole shape
The dimensions of each part can be read from the given side lengths of the compound shape
Different valid decompositions of the same shape are possible

lessons.title: Area of compound shapes
lessons.objective: Calculate the area of a compound shape made from rectangles by summing the areas of its rectangular parts.
must_establish: The area of a compound shape is the sum of the areas of its non-overlapping rectangular parts
Each part's area is found using area = length x width before summing
The total is expressed in square units

lessons.title: Choosing and justifying a method
lessons.objective: Choose a method to find the area of a compound rectangular shape and justify that it covers the whole shape without overlap or omission.
must_establish: A valid method accounts for every part of the shape exactly once
The choice of decomposition or subtraction method can be explained and checked against the shape
Different correct methods for the same shape give the same area
